title: Former ‘South Park’ Writer Launches Site to Expose Information About Cornell University Sexual Assault Case: ‘There Will Be Accountability’
description: Following the news that a former Cornell student had accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and none f
body:
Following the news that a former Cornell student had accused seven men of raping and drugging her at a frat house party in October 2024 — and none faced legal consequences — former “South Park” writer Toby Morton has launched a website dedicated to documenting the account of the woman (identified as Jane Doe), her lawsuit and the school’s response to the case.

	“I’m building this carefully, and it will take time,” wrote Morton on the site’s homepage. “I’ve already received names, photographs, documents, messages, and other information related to the case. Before publishing those materials, I want to make certain that every identity is correct, every photograph is of the right person. TheCornell7.org will bring together her account, the lawsuit, public records, documented reporting, institutional responses, and additional verified information as it becomes available.”
	

	He continued: “The goal is not to be first. The goal is to build a record that can withstand scrutiny. This will take time. It will be careful. It will be documented. And there will be accountability.”


	While much of the site remains under construction, Morton shared a separate statement to Instagram about his work, explaining that while he is “not a journalist,” that fact makes him “more dangerous.” “I have no limits, no boundaries, nobody to tell me I’ve gone too far,” he wrote.

	Information around the event has begun to surface following a lawsuit filed by the student against the college two weeks ago, which claimed that the school failed to protect her and prevent the alleged assault. At the time, following an investigation by the university, two of the men were expelled, while the other five received lesser punishment. The lawsuit claims that some of them were able to write essays to the school to reduce their disciplinary action, according to her attorney.
	

	On Sunday, Florence Pugh posted a statement on social media in response to the case, describing the incident as a “horrific act.” “I’m feeling uneasy and sick and anxious,” she wrote. “I’m processing quietly and watching everything and everyone and every man.”

	In addition to writing credits on “South Park,” Morton voiced Scott Tenorman on the show. He also wrote on “Mad TV.”

schema.headline: Former ‘South Park’ Writer Launches Site to Expose Information About Cornell University Sexual Assault Case: ‘There Will Be Accountability’

title: Rob Lowe Says ‘St. Elmo’s Fire’ Sequel Is Still ‘In the Works,’ Confirms There’s a Script: ‘All of Us Actors Want to Do It’
description:
Rob Lowe finally has an update on the long-discussed “St. Elmo’s Fire” sequel.

	“It is definitely in the works, for sure,” the actor said when aske
body:
Rob Lowe finally has an update on the long-discussed “St. Elmo’s Fire” sequel.

	“It is definitely in the works, for sure,” the actor said when asked about the project’s current status during a “Watch What Happens Live” appearance on Sunday. “All of us actors want to do it, and we’re supposed to get a draft of the script the first week of October.”

	While Lowe didn’t give much away, the news that the sequel is making progress is the latest update fans of the 1985 classic have been waiting on since the film was first announced in 2024. The “Parks and Recreation” actor told Entertainment Tonight that he’d “met with the studio” and had “been talking about doing it for about four months.” “But it’s very, very, very, very, very early stages,” he added. “So we will see.”
	

	That same year, Lowe’s “St. Elmo’s Fire” costar Demi Moore said that “conversations are happening” around the sequel, and revealed that discussions were underway with Sony, the same studio behind the original film. She also said the studio was “really behind [and] driving this,” though they were still “looking for the right partner” to write it.


	Variety previously reported that NBC was developing a series adaptation of the film back in 2019, though it never materialized. Josh Berman had been attached to write and executive produce, along with Chris King. At the time, the series was described as a modern adaptation of the film that showcases a group of close friends struggling with career, commitment and the responsibilities of adulthood.
	

	Released in 1985, “St. Elmo’s Fire” starred Lowe, Moore, Emilio Estevez, Andrew McCarthy, Ally Sheedy, Judd Nelson and others. Joel Schumacher directed and co-wrote the script with Carl Kurlander.

schema.headline: Rob Lowe Says ‘St. Elmo’s Fire’ Sequel Is Still ‘In the Works,’ Confirms There’s a Script: ‘All of Us Actors Want to Do It’

title: John Le Carré’s Cold War Spymaster George Smiley Returns in First Look at Matthew Macfadyen in ‘Legacy of Spies’
description: John Le Carré’s legendary British Cold War spy George Smiley, last seen on screens in the acclaimed film “Tinker Tailer Soldier Spy’ (played by Gary
body:
John Le Carré’s legendary British Cold War spy George Smiley, last seen on screens in the acclaimed film “Tinker Tailer Soldier Spy’ (played by Gary Oldman, coincidentally now starring as another fictitious agent in “Slow Horses”), has finally returned. 

	In the first image from BBC and MGM+ upcoming espionage thriller series “Legacy of Spies,” two-time Emmy and BAFTA winner Matthew Macfadyen appears in the iconic role. In another image, Charlie Hunnam is seen as the embattled, world-weary agent-runner and field operative Alec Leamas. 
	

	Filming has now wrapped on the eight-part series, which is adapted from le Carré’s bestseller “The Spy Who Came in From the Cold,” and drawing on material his 2017 novel “A Legacy of Spies.” Alongside Macfadyen and Hunnam, the show stars Daniel Brühl, Devrim Lingnau Islamoğlu, Agnes O’Casey, Felix Kammerer, Dan Stevens, Jake Dunn, Anjana Vasan, Charlotte Ritchie, Joe Alwyn and Hugh Laurie. Showrunners and writers are Stephen Cornwell (“Message from the King,” “A Most Wanted Man”) and Clarissa Ingram. Michael Lennox (“Say Nothing,” “Crystal Lake”) serves as an executive producer and had lead directorial duties.




	

					Charlie Hunnam as Alec Leamas in ‘Legacy of Spies’© The Ink Factory | Photographer Csaba Aknay
	



	In “Legacy of Spies,” when Leamas recruits Doris Quinz (Islamoğlu), a young and dynamic East German woman, to smuggle high-value Stasi documents into the West, it sets in motion a series of events that threaten to explode in the crucible of Cold War Berlin. Pursuing Leamas and Doris are Josef Fiedler (Brühl) and Hans-Dieter Mundt (Kammerer), two Stasi operatives whose ferocious desire to shut down the intelligence leak is matched only by their internal rivalry and an iron will to outmatch each other.
	

	Pulled into the action is Liz Gold (O’Casey), an idealistic young woman whose courage and conviction force Leamas to navigate a world where loyalties fracture and betrayal is inevitable. Behind the scenes, the brilliant and taciturn spymaster Smiley orchestrates operations while the elusive Soviet mastermind Karla looms in the shadows, setting the stage for a conflict that will define a generation. As per the description: “Personal lives become collateral in a ruthless intelligence war, and as the lines between duty and love begin to blur, every emotion becomes a weapon.”

	“Legacy of Spies” is set to launch exclusively on BBC iPlayer and BBC One in the U.K., and on MGM+ in the U.S., Germany, Spain, Italy, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands, Brazil and Spanish-speaking Latin America. The series will also air on SBS in Australia, Sky New Zealand and Sky Switzerland, and CANAL+ across France & French-speaking territories, Central & Eastern Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa.

	The series was filmed principally in the Czech Republic, with location filming also in the U.K. and Germany.

schema.headline: John Le Carré’s Cold War Spymaster George Smiley Returns in First Look at Matthew Macfadyen in ‘Legacy of Spies’

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Re-Release in the Works With New Footage
description: “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is getting a re-release with new footage, Variety has confirmed, although details about what’s in those new scenes remai
body:
“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is getting a re-release with new footage, Variety has confirmed, although details about what’s in those new scenes remain under wraps. A release date has also yet to be revealed. 

	“Brand New Day,” which launched July 31, was the box office story of the summer. The superhero blockbuster has grossed $2.49 billion at the domestic box office, making it the third highest-grossing movie of all time behind 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.92 billion) and 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.88 billion) and ahead of 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion) and 1994’s “Titanic” ($2.2 billion).
	

	On Sept. 16, “Brand New Day” eclipsed 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” as the highest-grossing domestic film of all time. “The Force Awakens” set the record at $936 million, a benchmark that had lasted more than a decade. “Spider-Man” took the crown after earning $936.773 million in just 47 days at North American cinemas.


	The last milestone left for the Marvel-Sony tentpole is to become the first movie to cross $1 billion at the domestic box office alone. “Brand New Day” currently sits at $950.6 million in North America, meaning the record most likely would be out of reach if it weren’t for the re-release.

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” follows Tom Holland’s Peter Parker as he tries to rebuild his life after a spell made his friends and family forget who he was. Other cast members include Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jon Bernthal, Jacob Batalon, Mark Ruffalo, Tramell Tillman and Florence Pugh. Destin Daniel Cretton directed the film with a screenplay by Chris McKenna and Erik Sommers.

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Re-Release in the Works With New Footage

title: Mohammad Rasoulof, O Mipo to Receive Tokyo Film Festival’s Kurosawa Akira Award
description: Mohammad Rasoulof, the Iranian filmmaker who secretly left his country in 2024 after being sentenced to eight years in prison, will receive the Kuro
body:
Mohammad Rasoulof, the Iranian filmmaker who secretly left his country in 2024 after being sentenced to eight years in prison, will receive the Kurosawa Akira Award at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival. He will share the honor with director O Mipo.

	The two were chosen by a committee of filmmakers Yamada Yoji and Lee Sang-il, cinematographer Ashizawa Akiko and TIFF programming director Ichiyama Shozo. Capcom Co., Ltd. backed the award’s return in 2022, after it had gone 14 years without being presented. Last year it went to Lee and Chloé Zhao.
	

	Rasoulof won the Golden Bear at Berlin in 2020 for “There Is No Evil,” which later played at the 33rd TIFF. His “The Seed of the Sacred Fig” took the Special Jury Prize at Cannes in 2024, and as Germany’s entry it was later nominated for the Oscar for best international feature. He was still finishing that film when he had to flee Iran in secret, shortly before Cannes. He was jailed in 2010 while shooting a film and arrested again in 2022, then provisionally released after eight months. He has shot many of his films in secret and smuggled them abroad to screen.


	The committee praised the “humanist perspective” of his recent work, “which portrays even those who perpetrate oppression as ordinary citizens.”

	“Receiving the Kurosawa Award is a great honor for me,” Rasoulof said. “His films are profound explorations of the human condition and the moral choices we make in moments of crisis.”

	O started out as a script supervisor after working at Obayashi Nobuhiko’s production company. She made her feature debut in 2006 with “The Sakais’ Happiness.” “The Light Shines Only There” (2014) won her best director at the Montreal World Film Festival and was Japan’s Oscar submission. “Being Good” (2015) was named best Asian film at the Moscow International Film Festival. After a nine-year gap in which she had two children, she came back with “Living in Two Worlds” (2024), which competed at Shanghai. Her latest, “How Dare You?” (2025), played in competition at Zlín.
	

	O said getting the award on the 20th anniversary of her debut left her grateful and humbled. “Winning the Shindo Kaneto Award in 2010 provided me with the vital support to keep making films. Though my progress has been slow, reaching the Kurosawa Akira Award is a stroke of fortune that makes me truly savor what a happy cinematic journey I have had,” she said.

	The festival will also show a selection of Kurosawa’s favorite films, along with two of his own. The lineup is Charles Chaplin’s “The Circus” (1928), 4K restorations of Kurosawa’s “Sanshiro Sugata” (1943) and “Ikiru” (1952), and Abbas Kiarostami’s “Where Is the Friend’s House?” (1987).

	Isomura, who won the Japan Academy Film Prize for best supporting actor for “The Moon,” will serve as jury president of the Ethical Film Award. Three members of TIFF’s student PR team will sit on the jury with him. The prize was set up with Sumitomo Corporation in 2023 and highlights films dealing with the environment, poverty, discrimination and diversity. This year’s nominees are Brenda Lígia’s “Amadeo and the Hypothetical New World” (Brazil), Isabelle Stever’s “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming” (Germany/Ukraine) and Vee Shi’s “Time and Tide” (Australia).

	Isomura said watching things on a small screen can fool people into thinking they understand something right away, when real understanding of social issues comes from working toward the answers. “Cinema possesses the unique power to pause our hurried pace, allowing us to experience that very process through the lives and emotions of others,” he said.

	Isomura also hosts the Shizuoka Film Festival in his hometown. His Netflix credits include “Alice in Borderland,” and Netflix will release his next project, “Did Someone Happen to Mention Me?” worldwide on Oct. 22. The Ethical Film Award will be presented on Nov. 2, along with a talk session with Isomura.

	The festival runs Oct. 26–Nov. 4. Its TIFFCOM market takes place Oct. 28–30.

schema.headline: Mohammad Rasoulof, O Mipo to Receive Tokyo Film Festival’s Kurosawa Akira Award

title: 'All American' Airs Series Finale Tonight: Here's How to Watch The CW Show's Final Episode Online Free
description:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	After eig
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	After eight seasons and more than 100 episodes, The CW‘s “All American” bids farewell tonight.

	The high school football drama airs its final episode tonight at 8 p.m. on The CW, closing a chapter that first premiered in October of 2018.

	Viewers can tune into the hour-long “All American” finale on TV through their local CW affiliate, or stream the show as it airs with a live streaming service like DIRECTV (currently offering a free trial here). DIRECTV carries a live CW feed that you can use to watch “All American” online free without cable.


	You can also watch the “All American” finale online through Fubo and Hulu + Live TV, both of which also offer free trials that let you watch the show on your computer, phone, tablet or smart TV. The final episode will be available to stream the next day on cwtv.com.

	Tonight’s series finale is titled “To Live and Die in L.A,” and welcomes back original cast members, Daniel Ezra (Spencer) and Samantha Logan (Olivia), as friends and family rally around Olivia as she goes into labor. Ezra also returned to direct the final episode.

	As Spencer James, Ezra played the main protagonist in the series, whose life in Crenshaw is turned on its head after he is recruited by coach Billy Baker (played by Taye Diggs) to play for a high school football team in Beverly Hills. The series followed the friendships and relationships made on and off the football field, while addressing themes of classism, adolescence and race.

	Diggs departed the show in a shocking season five episode, while original cast members Ezra, Logan, Cody Christian, Karimah Westbrook and Monet Mazur left at the end of season six. After a time jump, “All American” picked up in season seven with Greta Onieogou (Layla), Bre-Z (Coop) and Michael Evans Behling (Jordan) leading the cast along with a new group of regulars.


	Per an episode description, tonight’s series finale focuses on Spencer as he “navigates one of the toughest and most important days of his life. Meanwhile, Olivia leans on her mom to help her make the right decision. Friends and family, old and new, gather as one chapter ends and new chapters begin for our favorite Crenshaw and Beverly natives.” 

	The series finale episode is written by executive producer Nkechi Okoro Carroll along with co-showrunner Jamie Turner.

	Watch the “All American” series finale tonight at 8 p.m. ET/PT on The CW or stream it online free through DIRECTV. You can also watch all previous episodes of the show on Netflix or by purchasing it through Prime Video.

	“All American” is the last remaining scripted series on the CW that launched before the network’s sale to Nexstar. Okoro Carroll and Turner produce alongside Greg Berlanti, Sarah Schechter and David Strauss. The series — inspired by former NFL playe Spencer Paysinger — is produced by Warner Bros. Television and CBS Studios in association with Berlanti Productions.

schema.headline: 'All American' Airs Series Finale Tonight: Here's How to Watch The CW Show's Final Episode Online Free

title: Miley Cyrus Scores First No. 1 in Over a Decade on Albums Chart, While Ella Langley Extends Record on Singles Chart
description:
Miley Cyrus has scored her first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 in over a decade with her latest, “Bass Persuades.”

	The singer, who is going mon
body:
Miley Cyrus has scored her first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 in over a decade with her latest, “Bass Persuades.”

	The singer, who is going mononomously as Miley for this era, bows in the top spot with 61,000 equivalent album units. In a tight race, she landed ahead of Ella Langley‘s “Dandelion,” which holds at No. 2 with “nearly 61,000 units,” reports Billboard, followed by Riley Green at No. 3 with “That’s Just Me,” earning 60,000 units.
	

	Over on the Hot 100, Langley continues to mine chart gold as “Choosin’ Texas” earns a 24th week at No. 1, a week after breaking Mariah Carey’s record for most atop the tally with “All I Want For Christmas Is You.” Additionally, “Choosin’ Texas” breaks the record for most weeks at No. 1 (19) on the Digital Song Sales chart.


	“Bass Persuades” marks Cyrus’ sixth album to lead the Billboard 200, her last being “Bangerz” in 2013, and becomes her 16th overall project to reach the top 10. This makes her the third act in 2026 to have at least a decade between No. 1s, following Bruno Mars with “The Romantic” in March and A$AP Rocky with “Don’t Be Dumb” in January.

	She initially announced “Bass Persuades” in early September, just weeks before its arrival. “Music takes hold of us,” she wrote on social media in the announcement. “We feel it, sing it, sometimes dance to it, let it out and carry on. It is powerful, vulnerable, sweet and strong. Heart full, heartache, every part of life in between. That’s what the title means to me. Thank you for being a part of making my wildest dreams come true. I sincerely hope you love this album.”
	

	Cyrus then released the project’s title song and video as the first single, followed by the album on September 18. Next month, she’ll make a rare return to the stage with a two-night stint at Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles, performing on October 16 and 18. Model/Actriz, who is featured on “Bass Persuades,” will join her at the shows as a special guest.

	Rounding out the top five on the Billboard 200 are Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem” at No. 4 and Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” at No. 5. Spots six through 10 are Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide,” Beabadoobee’s “Pylon,” Jhené Aiko’s “Westside Whimsy,” Drake’s “Iceman” and Kahan’s “Stick Season.”

schema.headline: Miley Cyrus Scores First No. 1 in Over a Decade on Albums Chart, While Ella Langley Extends Record on Singles Chart

title: CBS and MTV VMAs Attract a Combined 8.4 Million Viewers, Making it the Most-Watched Since 2015 and Up 51% From Last Year
description: The Moon Man still has some life. CBS’ and MTV‘s coverage of the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards averaged a combined 8.43 million viewers on Sunday nigh
body:
The Moon Man still has some life. CBS’ and MTV‘s coverage of the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards averaged a combined 8.43 million viewers on Sunday night, according to Nielsen Live+same day fast nationals. Those numbers are subject to change once finals are in, but for now that makes it the most-watched VMAs in 11 years (since 2015, when it only ran on MTV) and puts it up 51% vs. last year’s show.

	The VMAs were likely assisted by an NFL football overrun (which went late until the Baltimore Ravens defeated the Dallas Cowboys), pushing the start time of the VMAs by several minutes (to 7:51 p.m. ET). The show still started at 4:30 p.m. PT inside L.A. Live’s Peacock Theater, but wound up being tape-delayed as a result on CBS.
	

	That 8.43 million number includes the simulcast on CBS and MTV, as well as an encore on MTV. But in an apples-to-apples comparison, the show last year (on Sept. 7, 2025) also aired on CBS, MTV and encored on MTV — and that telecast brought in 5.60 million viewers.


	In individual network numbers, the CBS telecast averaged 7.61 million viewers, up 52% from last year (5.00 million). MTV’s simulcast averaged 686,000 viewers (up 40% from last year’s 481,000). And the MTV encore brought in 142,000 viewers (up 31% from 108,000 last year).

	According to CBS, this year repped the best same-day audience for the VMAs since 2015, when the awards show hit a big 12.73 million viewers.

	In demos, this was the most-watched VMAs in adults 25-54 (3.11 million) since 2019 (3.55 million) and was up +34% from last year (2.32 million). In adults 18-49, the show took in 2.66 million — the best since 2018 (3.02 million) and up 32% from 2025 (2.02 million). And in adults 18-34, the show averaged 1/09 million, the best since 2020 (1.14 million) and up 46% from last year (751,000).
	

	CBS also reported social highlights: 31.1M interactions and 159M video views (up 8% from last year).

	The 2026 VMAs opened with Madonna — in her first VMAs performance in 23 years — with Sabrina Carpenter and Charli XCX. The show also featured Taylor Swift winning the video of the year award, taking the MTV VMA artist director award and premiering her new music video to “Patient Zero.”

	Also, Nirvana received the video vanguard award, and tributes were held for Dolly Parton and George Michael. Other performers included GENER8ION, Gunna, Kacey Musgraves, Lisa, Madonna, Raye, Shaboozey, Sienna Spiro, Sombr, Teddy Swims and Yung Lean.

	Snoop Dogg hosted the 2026 VMAs. Gunpowder & Sky produced the special, while. Van Toffler served as producer. Jesse Ignjatovic of Den of Thieves, Barb Bialkowski and Bruce Gillmer were executive producers alongside Barry Barclay and Floris Bauer. Melanie Block was co-executive producer and Gary Lanvy as co-producer. Snoop Dogg was executive producer alongside producers Sara Ramaker and Jasmin Ratansi. Jen Proctor was executive talent producer.

schema.headline: CBS and MTV VMAs Attract a Combined 8.4 Million Viewers, Making it the Most-Watched Since 2015 and Up 51% From Last Year

title: After a Booming Year, Horror Insiders Debate the Genre’s Future at Fantastic Fest: ‘You Can Take Big Swings and You’re Mitigating Your Risk’
description: 2026 was filled with visionary horror films that rocked the box office, like “Obsession” and “Backrooms.” But what does the future of the genre look
body:
2026 was filled with visionary horror films that rocked the box office, like “Obsession” and “Backrooms.” But what does the future of the genre look like?

	At this year’s Fantastic Fest in Austin, I moderated a panel about fear, fandom and the future of the horror genre, which touched on several topics about the business of getting scared. Joining me on the panel were Emily Gotto, Shudder‘s SVP of acquisitions and production; Nick Lazo, Shudder’s SVP of development and production; Angel Melanson, Shudder’s director of programming; Jordan Downey, the director of “The Cycle,” which debuted at Fantastic Fest, and a segment from the streamer’s “V/H/S/Beyond”; and Toby Poser, a member of the Adams Family filmmakers, whose “The Glorious Dead” played at Fantastic Fest and was recently announced to be acquired by Shudder.
	

	The conversation opened with thoughts about how horror has always been a space where filmmakers can take creative swings, experiment with form and push boundaries to do all kinds of fantastic work.

	“I think you can inherently take risks with scary material because you can have really deep conversations about dramatic things that happen in your life, and wrap them in this genre cloth that is accessible and fun and cool, but you’re also taking big swings with some material that may be too heavy-handed or otherwise a little difficult to swallow,” Lazo said. “I think the horror genre lends itself to emerging filmmakers and new voices and people who have something really compelling to say that don’t necessarily have access to the biggest budgets in the world. When you can say something very scary in a very dark room that doesn’t require a lot of lighting or set design or the most expensive cast that you can possibly bring to the table, you can take big swings and you’re mitigating your risk automatically just having your budget be a little bit lower.”
	

	The conversation then pivoted to other reasons for horror’s big boom this year.

	“I think horror is the best sandbox that you could possibly play in because, to Nick’s point, you can fold anything else into that,” Melanson said. “The rules are there are no rules. Horror dictates that you can do anything. You wrap fantasy in there, you can throw drama in there, you can have comedy. So you’re already opening yourself up to all these different things that you can layer within it. And I feel like everyone’s hungry for something that’s original, that’s new. And you look at the stuff that’s popping off right now and everyone is just very, very hungry and excited for these new and original concepts and ideas. Also, it’s very accessible. Equipment is becoming more accessible, but just horror inherently has always been a more accessible genre than something like going off to make a period drama that’s expensive. You can do more and I feel like it’s maybe a little bit more forgiving. You have strong performances, you have a strong story and we’re all going to show up for that.”

	At one point during the panel, Gotto was asked to predict what emerging themes or subgenres she thought could arrive in the next wave in horror.

	“Everybody loves a monster movie,” she said. “I think when we talk about originality, we’re talking about authorship. It’s the voice of the filmmaker that is coming forward to talk about something or someone within the genre sandpit. I love that term. Sometimes there can be very well-trodden themes and zeitgeists, but really what’s making something fresh is the point of view or the style of direction or the modes of talking about what is being brought to the fore, be it from a sociological, anthropological or individual subject matter, all of which I think are treated exceptionally well in genre. So in terms of new wave or next wave, I personally feel that that’s dictated by the filmmaker’s voices and the audience who’s willing to consume and celebrate those filmmakers’ voices. I don’t think it’s dictated by us as executives — or at least I would hope it’s not.”

	When it comes to how filmmakers’ voices can be influenced by the opinions of fans or reception at film festivals, Poser broke down how those opinions might impact the creative process.
	

	“We’re absolutely listening to what everyone has to say, and we almost take it as a personal challenge to then try something different,” she says. “For instance, sometimes people will say, ‘Oh, they do a lot of folk horror. They have slow burn.’ It was almost like homework with our newest one, ‘The Glorious Dead.’ We said, ‘No, let’s set out to really see what we do with a film that takes place over the course of one day with just escalating dread and a drive and momentum that we don’t usually focus upon.’ We love hearing what people think, and it almost grants us a responsibility to challenge ourselves as filmmakers and our audiences because we want to work. So we want to do a film pretty much every year or so. We have responsibility to them too to take what we learn and try new things.”

	Downey spoke specifically to how he processes instant feedback — like social media and Letterboxd reviews — when his art goes into the world.

	“It’s somewhat similar to feedback you get on a script or on a cut where you want to listen to it all, but then you try to build a bigger picture and not get too stuck on any one note or one comment, but you want to learn from it,” he said. “I feel like to be ignorant to it doesn’t really help you that much. And now live talking to people in person is a great way to do it, because people get online and just get into troll mode for unnecessary reasons sometimes. So I love talking to people right after the screening to hear what they thought. And I would also love if someone said, ‘Hey, I didn’t really like this scene or this moment.’ But it’s just like notes on anything where you just take it all with a grain of salt and ultimately have to filter it through your own filmmaking style and just move on to the next one and try to do better.”

schema.headline: After a Booming Year, Horror Insiders Debate the Genre’s Future at Fantastic Fest: ‘You Can Take Big Swings and You’re Mitigating Your Risk’

title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Star Alan Cumming Says ‘I Don’t Fully Understand the Plot’ and Only Acted With Florence Pugh’s Stunt Double
description: Alan Cumming is starring in “Avengers: Doomsday” but told SiriusXM point blank: “To be honest, I don’t fully understand the plot.” Not that Marvel a
body:
Alan Cumming is starring in “Avengers: Doomsday” but told SiriusXM point blank: “To be honest, I don’t fully understand the plot.” Not that Marvel allowed the returning “X-Men” star to read the full screenplay to the comic book tentpole, but even filming his scenes left Cumming with zero clarity on what was going on around him. The Emmy winner said his purpose in the movie boiled down to just running around. 

	“There was a bit when we were shooting a scene, and it was one of the rare scenes when I was actually on the backlot and not in front of a blue screen,” Cumming said. “And this man came and said, ‘So right now Alan, these giant robots are blah blah,’ and started to tell me the thing, and I was like, ‘You know what, thank you so much, but just tell me where I point my, whatever I point. And I’ll do that. Really, I just know I’m here to run around.'”
	

	“And I saw Florence Pugh yesterday at the Emmys,” he added. “And I said, ‘Gosh, it’s so funny. I’ve never met you, but you lay on top of me, or your body double did.’ And she goes, ‘Yeah I lay on top of you as well, but it was your body double.'”

	Cumming reprises the mutant Nightcrawler in “Avengers: Doomsday” alongside returning “X-Men” stars Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, Rebecca Romijn and James Marsden. He debuted as the mutant in “X2: X-Men United” but did not appear in any other “X-Men” movie, making “Doomsday” the first time he’s gotten the chance to play the character in 23 years. He previously said advancements in movie makeup dramatically cut back the amount of time he spent transforming into the blue-skinned and tattooed Nightcrawler.
	

	“Before it was about four and a half hours to apply it, but now it’s only 90 minutes,” Cumming explained. “Before, all of the tattoos were done by hand. They hadn’t decided on them before we started filming. Now, they just stick onto my face. It’s a game changer.”

	“Avengers: Doomsday” opens in theaters Dec. 18. Watch Cumming’s full interview with SiriusXM in the video below.

schema.headline: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Star Alan Cumming Says ‘I Don’t Fully Understand the Plot’ and Only Acted With Florence Pugh’s Stunt Double

            Presley Gerber was high before entering the sober house where he died, and the facility knew he was under the influence but still let him in ... sources tell TMZ.
      
    
            Multiple sources, one with direct knowledge, tell TMZ ... the afternoon before Presley's death, a member of his sober team called Resolutions Living saying they wanted to take Presley to the facility's sober house, but wanted to know if the staff would take him, because he was "high."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The staff responded ... bring him in.
      

            As TMZ previously reported, Pressley arrived shortly after 6 PM while under the influence of a substance.
      
    
            We're told he was acting erratically and making troubling comments about why he had gotten high.
      
    
            Nick Mathews, the owner of a drug and treatment center, tells TMZ ... "As a cardinal rule, a sober living facility that is not licensed and is ill-equipped to handle a detoxing patient should not take any client who is using."
      
    
            As we also reported, people close to Pressley say a doctor was providing him with ketamine, despite knowing he was a drug addict.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We reached out to the owner of Resolutions Living, but did not hear back.
      
    
            As far as cause of death, toxicology is pending ... but we're told authorities believe he died of an overdose.

title: Hayden Panettiere’s Ex Wladimir Klitschko Files For Temporary Guardianship of Daughter
description:
Hayden Panettiere
                          Ex Wladimir Klitschko Files For Temporary Guardianshi
body:
Hayden Panettiere
                          Ex Wladimir Klitschko Files For Temporary Guardianship ...
                          Fears Late Actress's Property is at Risk
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 28, 2026
                
                            11:03 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 28, 2026
                                3:50 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden Panettiere's ex Wladimir Klitschko is asking a court to name him guardian of his daughter Kaya in order to protect her rights as the sole beneficiary of Hayden's estate ... and saying he's concerned that some of the late actress’s assets may be lost, TMZ has learned. 
      
    
            In his petition to be appointed as temporary guardian, Wladimir says Kaya is "not a resident of California; this Court has jurisdiction over the guardianship of Kaya's estate because, as such heir, Kaya is entitled to the entirety of the assets subject to Hayden's probate administration in California."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            In the petition, obtained by TMZ, he says federal agents accessed Hayden's home as part of an ongoing investigation and removed her property. He wants to be the rep for the estate so he can get the property back when the probe is over. 
      

            Hayden's ex says in the papers that before she died, Hayden hired a security service to protect her home and its contents, "arising from a documented concern that an individual had gained unauthorized access to Hayden's property."
      
    
            He says locks were changed by a company following Hayden's death, "and storage units containing designer clothing and accessories worn to public appearances have been relocated as a precaution."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            He says "it is expected that the individual will continue to try and misappropriate property belonging to Hayden's estate. Given the high publicity of Hayden's estate, a personal representative needs to be appointed immediately to safeguard and protect Hayden's home and contents."
      
    
            Kaya will not only inherit the items seized or missing ... but because Hayden died without a will ... she will be the sole heir to all of her property, including her WeHo condo.
      
    
            Hayden died on August 16 at the age of 36.
